title: Flow-Gating Tailline Sculptor: admission flow-gating and batch-shape tuning to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: We continue to see 99.9th percentile decode latency spikes for small interactive requests during microbursts. Investigation shows bursty arrivals interacting poorly with current admission logic and kernel selection heuristics: short sequences are admitted into large-batch paths that pick suboptimal attention kernels and then contend for prefill slots, causing long tail decode stalls.

Goal: Implement a flow-gating layer that (1) classifies arriving requests into shape-stable microstreams, (2) enforces admission windows to avoid kernel contention, and (3) reshapes admission targets for prefill vs decode so short requests get low-latency kernel paths while long streaming requests trade throughput. We expect a 30-50% reduction in 99.9th percentile latency on measured microburst workloads without regressing median throughput more than 5%.
acceptance_criteria: QA: 99.9th percentile decode latency reduced by >=30% on internal microburst benchmark compared to baseline
Benchmark: median token throughput drop <=5% on mixed workload (10% long streaming, 90% short interactive)
Behavior: short inference requests (<64 tokens) are routed to low-latency kernel variants and bounded-prefill windows are applied
Observability: dashboard shows new metrics (flow_id, admission_bucket, kernel_variant) and trace spans for admission decisions
Rollout: feature gated by runtime flag and A/B rollout with automatic rollback on latency regressions
design_notes: Flow identification: compute a stable flow_id using (customer_id, model_version, route, hashed prompt fingerprint) to group similar shapes without exposing PII

Admission windows: sliding-window token budget per flow that enforces a soft cap and a hard cap. Soft cap triggers early kernel selection for low-latency path; hard cap rejects or defers admission to next window
Kernel hints: admission layer emits kernel_hint metadata to the scheduler (e.g., small-attention, kv-optimized) to bias kernel selection for admitted batches

Prefill vs decode shaping: maintain two admission queues per flow (prefill_queue, decode_queue). New requests first evaluated for prefill budget — prefer short requests for decode_queue to minimize latency
Backpressure strategy: incrementally increase admission deferral probability for flows that exceed soft cap, prefer graceful deferral over full rejection
Compatibility: compatible with existing continuous batching runtime; admission decisions are made pre-kv-cache allocation to avoid wasted cache reservations
Fallback: if kernel_hint not supported on target node, route to fallback kernel with a logged metric (kernel_hint_miss)
tradeoffs: Increased scheduling complexity and metrics cardinality vs measurable tail latency reduction
Potential small throughput regressions due to stricter shaping for short requests — accepted up to 5% median throughput drop
Flow grouping risks: overly aggressive grouping could starve individual low-volume tenants; conservative hashing chosen to avoid cross-customer mixing
Kernel hinting reduces perfect packing efficiency but reduces long-tail stalls from kernel contention
test_plan: Unit tests for flow_id hashing and admission window logic
Integration tests that simulate microburst traffic mixes with deterministic timing to validate admission deferral behavior
End-to-end benchmark using the existing microburst harness (github: redwood-infra/microburst-bench#34) to measure p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies
Chaos test: randomly flip kernel_hint availability to validate fallback and metric emission
Canary in staging: enable feature for 5% of traffic and run for 48 hours with automatic traffic ramping and rollback triggers based on tail latency
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal canary): rollout to internal dev org only, gather traces and tune window sizes (1 week)
Phase 2 (staging canary): 5% production-simulated load in staging, run microburst benchmark and validate dashboards (3 days)
Phase 3 (gradual production): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with automated regression detection on p99/p999
Rollback policy: immediate rollback if p999 increases by >10% for >30 minutes or error rate >0.5%
Post-rollout: 2-week observation, then bake changes into runtime-1.24 if stable
